Amazon says its exposure to exchange rates has grown as it has expanded internationally. In 2025, FX raised net sales by $4.4 billion. Its disclosed FX effects on operating income were mixed: $204 million negative, $903 million positive and $341 million negative. A hypothetical 5% adverse FX move would reduce the value of its $29.7 billion of foreign funds by about $1.5 billion, and a 20% move by $5.9 billion. In Q2 2026, FX had no significant effect on net sales. For the six months, it added $3.0 billion.
Amazon's risk factors say that as it has expanded its international operations, its exposure to exchange rate fluctuations has increased. It repeats this in the Q2 2026 10-Q.
Amazon warns that when the U.S. Dollar strengthens against the relevant currencies, its foreign-currency cash equivalents and marketable securities balances, once translated, may be materially less than expected, and vice versa. The Q2 2026 10-Q adds foreign-denominated note balances and payments to this list.
Sensitivity (FY2025 10-K, Item 7A): based on foreign funds of $29.7 billion at December 31, 2025, an assumed 5%, 10% and 20% adverse change in foreign exchange would reduce them by $1.5 billion, $3.0 billion and $5.9 billion.
FY2025 net sales: Amazon reported that changes in foreign exchange rates increased net sales by $4.4 billion in 2025. They reduced North America net sales by $454 million.
FY2025 operating income: the 10-K MD&A reports FX effects of a $204 million negative, a $903 million positive and a $341 million negative impact on operating income in 2025. These are reported across segments, so FX moves can push results in different directions.
Latest quarter: Amazon said FX did not significantly impact net sales for Q2 2026 but increased net sales by $3.0 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2026. FX increased North America net sales by $139 million in Q2 2026 and by $485 million for the six months.
Amazon provides FX-effect information to show reported operating results as if exchange rates had remained the same as in the comparable prior-year period.
